title: Synaptic plasticity
prompt:
Create a 30-second silent English 1920×1080 educational animation about Synaptic plasticity for Introduction to Neuroscience.
Use Remotion 4.0.410, React 19 and the introduction-to-neuroscience course kit. Reproduce the actual video in assets/source-kits/introduction-to-neuroscience/src/videos/ns09-synaptic-plasticity.tsx; fps is 30.
Keep the same dark course palette and diagrams. Use the actual state transitions from the source, not a generic neural-network animation.

Scene plan:
1. 0–6s, test: Pulse reaches synapse and produces an EPSP of relative amplitude 1 Why: Baseline synaptic efficacy converts input to response Visible result: Store the original EPSP as a dashed comparison
2. 6–11s, induction: Several pulses arrive; a recruitment signal travels toward the receptor pool Why: Suitable activity can initiate plasticity signaling Visible result: A visible trigger precedes membrane modification
3. 11–18s, insertion: Three individually tracked receptors move from intracellular pool into membrane slots; count grows 3 to 6 and efficacy grows 1 to 2 Why: Additional functional AMPA receptors increase postsynaptic responsiveness Visible result: Pool decreases as membrane collection increases; no receptor teleports
4. 18–25s, retest: Equal input pulse generates a new EPSP twice the illustrative baseline height Why: Synapse changed while test input stayed fixed Visible result: Overlay exposes a larger response without enlarging the incoming pulse
5. 25–30s, persistence: Another equal test evokes the strengthened EPSP while receptors remain inserted Why: Potentiation persists beyond the inducing activity Visible result: Memory of prior activity is expressed as efficacy, not a stronger test

All on-screen labels and narration-equivalent captions are concise English. Use no spoken audio or music. Preserve the specific objects, state bindings and timing above. Render the registered composition for this slug and inspect the final MP4 at the stored risk moments.
Reproduction requires the packaged TSX source, the course kit, Remotion/React dependencies, Chromium and ffmpeg. This prompt describes the reviewed artifact; it is not a self-contained promise of pixel-identical reproduction without those files.
final_title: Synaptic Plasticity: Stronger Response, Same Input
learning_objective: Explain how adding postsynaptic AMPA receptors can strengthen a synapse so the same test input evokes a larger EPSP.
core_conclusion: Synaptic plasticity changes response strength; AMPA receptor insertion is one mechanism of potentiation.

requirement_prompt:
Create a 15-second silent educational animation in Manim Community Edition.

Explain “Synaptic plasticity” using this visual metaphor: “a glowing neural circuit carrying one signal for Synaptic plasticity”. Dynamically demonstrate the core formula or conclusion: Synaptic plasticity changes connection strength with activity..

Use one continuous scene and one clear narrative line. Explain only this concept; do not add comparisons, extensions, or side cases. Structure the motion in three connected beats:
1. 0–3 seconds: establish the objects, input, or initial state.
2. 3–10.95 seconds: show at least two causally connected state changes that reveal the mechanism and progressively connect key variables or conclusions to the visual.
3. 10.95–12.45 seconds: resolve the result, invariant, or central insight.

Keep introducing meaningful animation information until 12.45 seconds. Hold the final still frame for no more than 2.55 seconds.

All on-screen titles, labels, and supporting annotations must be short English phrases in Arial. Use a bright, non-black background (#EEF7EE); main visual (#145A56); secondary visual (#8F2B2B); highlight (#735000); and text (#172033). Maintain strong contrast and legibility.

Strict typography requirements:
- Render every complete title, label, phrase, or sentence as one native Text(...) object so every character shares one baseline.
- Never rebuild a line from separately positioned word or letter objects, and never align words by their individual bounding boxes.
- Create Arial text at a base font_size of 64, then uniformly scale the complete Text object to its final visual size; do not render explanatory text directly at a tiny font size.
- Preserve ordinary spaces inside the same Text object, set disable_ligatures=True, and do not add manual tracking, special-width spaces, or per-character offsets.

Use ThreeDScene for a genuinely spatial main visual: at least one core object must show volume, depth, or occlusion, and include one smooth camera move that reveals spatial structure. The 3D motion must clarify the concept rather than merely tilt a flat diagram. Render in 16:9.

Global rendering requirements:
- Never place plain English words, sentences, titles, or explanatory prose in MathTex, Tex, or inline LaTeX math mode. Use the native Text(...) component for all explanatory text and titles.
- If an English word is unavoidable inside a mathematical expression, explicitly wrap every word with \text{...}; never leave a word bare in algebra mode.
- Animate text at whole-word or whole-line granularity. Never split text into individually spaced letters or animate isolated letter spans.
- Do not use text-align: justify or the SVG textLength or lengthAdjust attributes.
- Use the final conclusion display as the video's opening poster frame; do not begin on an empty background.

production.scene_rationale: Five scenes distinguish baseline testing, induction, receptor insertion, matched retesting and persistence. The separate insertion scene is needed to show a material membrane change rather than declare LTP; the second test controls input strength.

critical_processes.uncertainty: Membrane receptor count must change only when moving receptors reach their slots, and output must depend on the same strength state.
critical_processes.expected_observation: Receptors physically enter membrane; matched later pulse creates larger EPSP.

bindings.strength: SynapticWeight strength and EPSP path amplitude

assertions: Before insertion: 3 membrane + 3 pool receptors, strength 1.
During insertion: each receptor has one position and total tracked population remains 6.
Matched tests retain input=1 and response=input*strength.

observations.observed: Baseline has three membrane receptor bars and response 1.0. Inducing-activity stage retains those three while a presynaptic marker advances.

Yellow receptor bars leave the right-side pool and occupy positions progressively nearer the membrane. Later frames show five membrane receptors and response 1.7, then six receptors and response 2.0. The blue EPSP curve becomes taller than the retained dotted baseline.

The equal test input is still labeled 1.0 and its marker moves along the input segment. Six membrane receptors, doubled response and taller current EPSP persist during retest and the later 28 s condition.
